warnings.warning: Several printed polar area or margin formulas conflict with standard area or arc-length relations; retain them as source evidence rather than reusable validated geometry.
The growth-rate expression is described as the derivative of equation 1 rather than equation 16, and its regression evidence and margin descriptor are not independently documented.
The black-radiation expression has unclear dimensions and constants, while the later reaction system omits calibration, initial conditions, and a defined product-to-energy unit mapping.
Equation 32 is recursively printed and is not algebraically executable as written; the cell-flux to whole-tree transport handoff is also undefined.
The cited four-compartment Darcy model is reduced to xylem flow without a reduction-error contract, measured inputs, or a tree-scale aggregation rule.
The circumcircle and concavity corrections have no bounded approximation error, and pairwise overlap subtraction can double-count regions shared by more than two leaves.

The branch relation does not preserve the cumulative-angle dependence of the preceding torque equation; the wind term also lacks standard velocity-squared scaling and a dimensional coefficient definition.

The physiological tree equations contain unestimated coefficients and undefined aggregation from prior submodels, so they do not produce the reported tree height under a reproducible parameterization.

The structural bending and gravity expressions have unresolved dimensional semantics, and the crown-volume table is internally inconsistent; keep the downstream mass outputs source-faithful but unendorsed.

global_organization_chain: Summary states the organ-interaction gap and previews a leaf-to-tree modeling staircase.
Introduction makes the staircase operational through leaf taxonomies, four requested relation levels, and a four-section roadmap.
The model chapter formalizes leaf shape, growth, and three physiological processes before moving to arrangement, branching, and tree characteristics.

Shared concepts create the handoffs: margin length enters growth, light absorption motivates overlap, physiological products feed the tree equations, and branch geometry feeds volume, height, and mass.
Solutions and Results revisit the same branches in question order and attach each to a regression, field comparison, torque table, or structural estimate.
The leaf-mass branch preserves the unusable physiological comparison and reports the structural alternative rather than hiding the failed route.
Discussion reviews leaf-level contributions, then cross-scale relations, and closes with the ideal isolated-system boundary and unmodeled ecosystem factors.

main_argument_chains.claim: Leaf-shape differences can be represented as adjustable geometric objects and linked to growth and physiological processes.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Reuse the shape-to-process architecture only with explicit model scope and without promoting the reported visual fits to independent validation.
support_steps: Bound the retained leaf classes and map them to polar functions.
Distinguish the cell-division margin from the blade perimeter before it enters the growth coefficient.
Adapt the logistic growth relation and derive the daily growth rate.
Split physiology into photosynthesis, transportation, and transpiration and state their structure-to-function links.
Compare growth and photosynthesis outputs with the reported regression figures and transportation output with a field-data graph.

main_argument_chains.claim: The same light-absorption objective connects physiological modeling to leaf arrangement and overlap geometry.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The conceptual handoff is reusable, while the circumcircle approximation and field-data provenance remain explicit evidence boundaries.
support_steps: State light absorption as the photosynthesis-stage guideline.
Forward-reference that principle when opening the arrangement section.
Use a two-dimensional projection baseline and add incidence angle for the three-dimensional branch.
Standardize leaf shapes to computable circle intersections.
Compare calculated and field shadow areas for four arrangement cases and retain every displayed error.

main_argument_chains.claim: Leaf properties are connected to branch and tree characteristics through mechanics and structural aggregation.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Preserve the cross-scale output chain, but keep all magnitudes conditional on the recorded dimensional and parameter warnings.
support_steps: Represent branch development with the LA rod system and select wind as an environmental forcing.
Relate leaf effective area to wind force and branch torque.
Compare wind and gravity moments with measured branch angles.
Rotate branch platforms to estimate crown volume and height.
Use bending-moment equilibrium to estimate branch and total leaf mass.

main_argument_chains.claim: The paper's strongest evidence-handling move is to abandon an untestable physiological leaf-mass branch and report a structural alternative.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Use feasibility gates and negative results to select a branch without claiming that the replacement validates the rejected model.
support_steps: Set physiological and structural approaches against the same tree outputs.
Identify unavailable coefficients as a feasibility blocker in the model chapter.
Report that available physiological experiments are inconsistent and highly variable.
Withhold that model test instead of converting the noisy results into support.
Proceed with the structural table while preserving its separate evidence limitations.

visualization_dispositions.analytical_purpose: Shape, venation, and arrangement figures provide taxonomy scaffolding, not model validation.
Polar plots make parameterized shape families inspectable, but black and green boundary semantics and fitted data are not consistently explained.
A composite photosynthesis diagram is imported as context and does not visualize the paper's state variables or interfaces.
Overlap diagrams clarify the circle approximation and pair geometry.
The crown-platform schematic makes the structural surrogate understandable and labels its equivalent geometry.
Validation figures omit residuals, uncertainty, source-data overlay, and quantitative network comparison.
